title: Attributes
goal: In this lesson you will learn how attributes store data on each object, using a dot.
learn: Each object keeps its own values
idea: An attribute is a piece of data stuck on an object. You set it with a dot, like dog.name = "Buddy", and you read it the same way with print(dog.name). Each object can have different attribute values even when they share a class.
changeOneLine: In the editor above, change dog1.age = 3 to dog1.age = 5 and press Run. The first line should say Buddy is 5.

practice.text: Make a Pet, set name and kind, print both.
practice.hint: Set pet.kind to a string in quotes, like "cat" or "hamster". Then use print(pet.name) and print(pet.kind).

pet.kind =

practice.text: Make two Players with different levels. Print both levels.
practice.hint: The levels are already set on a and b. Print each player's level with print(a.level) and print(b.level).
practice.starterTip: Fill the two print() lines with print(a.level) and print(b.level). You should see 2 then 7.
practice.starter:
class Player:
    pass
a = Player()
b = Player()
a.level = 2
b.level = 7
print()
print()
practice.gradingNote: Pass if 2 and 7 print from attributes.

quiz.question: How do you set an attribute?
quiz.correct: Right, you use a dot and then assign.

quiz.question: Do dog1.age and dog2.age have to match?

options.text: No. Each object has its own

quiz.correct: Yes, attributes belong to each object separately.

quiz.question: How do you read an attribute?
quiz.correct: Right, you read it with the same dot syntax.
